newsitem.title: USA: American States up amid takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: American States up amid takeover talk.

text.p: Shares of American States Financial Corp rose about three percent Friday amid speculation that the company may be for sale and that SAFECO Corp may be a possible buyer.

SAFECO declined comment. American States, which is up about 18 percent since February, said it does not comment on market speculation. However, the company noted that its shares are thinly traded and subject to volatility.
American States rose one to 33-3/8 on about twice the average daily volume.
Lincoln National Corp , which has an 83 percent stake in American States, also declined comment on the speculation.

But, Lincoln National did not rule out a possible sale of its stake in the future. "All options are open," a Lincoln National spokesman said. "We look at opportunities as they come and we don't preclude anything," he said.
Speculation about a possible takeover of American States picked up steam late last month after ReliaStar Financial Corp agreed to buy Security-Connecticut Corp, a former Lincoln States holding.

After that deal was announced, CS First Boston analyst Charles Gates made comments to the firm's sales force, noting that American States is the only Lincoln National spinoff left that has not yet been acquired.
National Re, formerly owned by Lincoln National, was bought last summer by General Re Corp.
Emphesys Financial Group Inc, also a former Lincoln National business, was sold in 1995 to Humana Inc.
Analysts said they believed Lincoln National was unlikely in the long-term to hold onto its American States stake.
But, they said, they were unsure whether Safeco was a logical buyer of the business.
One analyst said Safeco was not known as a consolidator and said the recent runup in the stock price of American States might discourage it from making a bid.

However, even though Safeco has not been acquisitive in the past, competitive issues may prompt it to take action over the next year or so, Merrill Lynch analyst Michael Frinquelli wrote in a January research report.
Another industry source said he believed the purchase of American States might make sense for Safeco.
American State's middle market commercial property-casualty business, he said, would blend well with its current commercial and personal property-casualty business.
